items.text: Sliders in the heads-up panes, flyouts and rows follow the Surface standard: a slim line, a round handle, the readout white at its default and in the accent once changed. A double-tap on a slider or its readout glides it back to its default with a small pulse (Surface Reset).
The vertical slider in a flyout has room at its foot.
The Binaural beat section of the heads-up display wears the same headphones icon as its button, so you can tell where you landed.

Controls that open a heads-up pane when you hold them (sound load, binaural, the crossfader's motion) carry a small triangle in the upper right, the way the rail's lower left triangle marks a submenu.
The flyout of the last button in a group, or one low on the screen (the heads-up button), now rises from the button's own level and opens upward.

A saved look now remembers its binaural beat: on or off, the preset (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Tempo), the level and the source. Applying a look, or a performance movement with a look, sets them. Opening the page still never switches a beat on.

A sixteen-column score now fits the frame on a phone (it ran past the stage and under the side rail). Opening a piece switches the A|B habits sweep (and its roll at each edge) off, so it cannot swing the colours or add scenes to the piece.

Make a piece from your scenes (Performance, at the foot, under Pieces): name it and every scene you have, in order, becomes a performance of movements, the same as an opened piece. It keeps the grids, scale, tempo and the way lines run. Save it in My sets or copy it as text and the scenes travel with it. It needs at least two scenes of the same grid size.

Pieces now live in the Performance section (under Pieces, at the foot): Bach, Satie, the two drum studies, or a MIDI file of your own. Opening one makes a performance of movements, eight scenes each, with the source named. Save it as a set or copy it as text and it carries its piece; a movement that begins puts the piece on its first scene, so the clock and the music stay together.
The Colour habits box keeps only "Read habits from the piece".

Open a MIDI file (Colour habits box, "A piece of music"), or try one of four: Bach's Contrapunctus I, Satie's Gymnopédie No. 1, and two drum studies in the style of Haitian djouba and Lebanese dabke. Each track becomes a colour and the piece becomes scenes (16 steps each) that play one after another; "Play through" switches that off, "Back to the start" returns.
"Read habits from the piece" sets the colour sliders from every note of the whole piece, so new scores can be rolled in its manner. Habits carry register, spread and share, not harmony or phrase.
It is Battanboo's reading, not a re-performance: pitch is spread over the piece's own range onto 16 lanes, and when two tracks land in one cell the louder note stays (the count is told).
The A to B habits slider takes a MIDI knob, and the habits animator takes a pad (tap the MIDI button, then the shape).
A Performance movement's look now includes the colour habits and both poses, so each section can start with its own character.

Read habits from what was heard: every note is now logged with its pitch lane, and Colour habits and Statistics can read "from what was heard" as well as from the score (notes tapped by hand are not read).

Analysis is now careful with the sound: reading habits is done in slices of a few milliseconds (it took 13 ms in one go on a fast computer, so would have been more on a phone), only when asked, and it pauses by itself while a Performance runs or the device is busy. Notes are still logged. "Always analyse" keeps it going.
